  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  MARCH 25, 2025

  A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Negrete at 5:31 p.m., on
  Tuesday, March 25, 2025, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

  Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Lana Negrete
  Mayor Pro Tem Caroline Torosis (Arrived at 5:34 PM)
  Councilmember Jesse Zwick
  Councilmember Dan Hall
  Councilmember Ellis Raskin
  Councilmember Barry Snell
  Councilmember Natalya Zernitskaya

  City Attorney Douglas Sloan
  City Clerk Nikima S. Newsome

  CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:31 p.m., with all
  members present except Mayor Pro Tem Torosis. Councilmember
  Zernitskaya led the assemblage in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica is located on the land of Tovangaar. With
  ACCOUNTABILITY  great respect, the City acknowledges the Gabrieleño/Tongva as the First
  (LAND  People of this ancestral and unceded territory of Kuruvungna, a village
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)  that we know as Santa Monica. We honor their elders, past and present,
  and the Gabrieleño descendants who are part of the Gabrieleño /Tongva
  tribes.

  We recognize that these peoples are still here, and as settlers and kuyam
  (guests), we recognize our responsibility and obligation to care for their
  land in partnership with them. The City of Santa Monica commits to
  work in partnership with the Gabrieleño/Tongva people to uplift their
  voices and visibility on their ancestral land.

  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember Zwick.

  DISCLOSURE  permit, license, contract, or other entitlement before the Council is
  required to disclose on the record any contribution, including
  aggregated contributions, of more than $500 made by the party or the

  Questions asked and answered of staff included is the continuance of the low
  income assistance program and other ancillary programs projected in the
  budget; what are the risks of deferring maintenance; how much more could
  deferred maintenance possibly cost; what is the process for coming back to
  Council should the costs increase and how does the city know that rate

  Ficus tree roots built into the water rate increase and is this an ongoing issue.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to the
  availability of an app for residents to monitor their water; the quality of the
  city’s water system resulting in it not being affected by the Palisades Fire;
  the benefits of selecting option 1 in the staff report; and the importance of
  having clean, safe potable water as the climate crisis intensifies.

  Third Street Promenade Area, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Sections
  15301 (Existing Facilities, 15303 (New Construction or Conversion
  of Small Structures), and 15311 (Accessory Structures) of the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.
  2. Introduction for first reading of an Interim Zoning Ordinance
  Amending Interim Zoning Regulations Established to Promote
  Economic Recovery by Increasing Land Use Flexibility in the City’s
  Downtown Area and Establishing a Pilot Program to Allow for
  Exclusively Commercial Outdoor Uses in the Office Campus District
  to Allow Additional Flexibility Related to Community Assembly
  Uses in the Bayside Conservation District.
  3. Introduction and Adoption of an Emergency Ordinance Amending
  Santa Monica Municipal Code Chapter 9.61: Signs to Make Minor
  Changes for Signage in the Bayside Conservation District and Third
  Street Promenade Area to Promote Economic Recovery.

  Member of the public Denise Barton, spoke to the recommended action.

  8  March 25, 2025
 Docusign Envelope ID: 900E3178-25A7-40CD-AE38-1F4E679CB055

  Questions asked and answered of staff included why is the city choosing
  make the width of digital signage to be 100% as opposed to 90%; concerns
  about the brightness of the signage and the time period; are there many multi-
  tenant commercial buildings that could have multiple animated digital signs;
  are there any best practices are recommendations to angle the signs down to
  avoid light pollution; would the signs be permitted to have sound; is the size
  in this proposal smaller than what was previously allowed; is the proposal
  for the signs to only be permitted to face the Promenade; what is the
  advantage of this to remain temporary and not permanent; addressing
  concerns raised by the Fire Chief; and are the maximum brightness, ambient
  light, dimmable requirements, etc. in line with other shopping districts
  throughout the region.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to the
  elimination of restrictions providing greater flexibility of uses for community
  assembly uses; creating safer spaces with the presence of more people in the
  streets; tying light hours to closing hours for safety concerns; the importance
  of facilitating economic opportunity and growth at the Promenade while also
  maintaining brightness standards; moving to make these temporary measures
  permanent; and the ability for the city or Downtown Santa Monica to
  coordinate special lighting events.

  Motion by Mayor Pro Tem Torosis, seconded by Mayor Negrete, to adopt
  the staff recommendation. The motion was approved by the following vote:
